paras: The McLauren family killings took place on the afternoon of Tuesday, April 19, 1881, when a party of about fifteen armed men rode to the house of a man named McLauren on the Frio in Edwards County, Texas, and killed McLauren, his wife and a young man named Lease who lived with them. No motive, accusation or suspect for the killings was reported, and nothing in the house was taken. Papers across the country carried the story as a 'mysterious triple murder'.

According to a dispatch from Uvalde dated April 21, a party of fifteen men rode up to McLauren's house on Tuesday afternoon and took the lives of McLauren, his wife and the young man. Everything in the household was left undisturbed, which a St. Louis special took to mean that plunder 'evidently, was not the object'. The news reached Uvalde through people living in that neighborhood, and the first dispatch noted that particulars had not yet been received.
None of the reports stated the race of the victims or of the attackers. Nor do they say how the three were killed.

A San Antonio Express special from Uvalde added that evidence was accumulating against Logan, Humphreys and Rawley, three young men recently arrested for robbing the Corpus Christi stage, though it did not say that this evidence concerned the killings. No report of an arrest, inquest or trial for the McLauren killings appears in the coverage, and a Wisconsin weekly said a week later that 'The affair remains a mystery.'

Coverage came only from white papers and began on April 22 with the Dallas Herald's special from Uvalde, which the paper's weekly edition reprinted word for word on April 28. Also on April 22, a St. Louis special that gave the place as the 'little town of Trio' ran under the headline 'CONCERTED MURDER' in the Rock Island Argus, and the next day the Los Angeles Herald printed it as 'A Cold-Blooded Slaughter'. A third version, the San Antonio Express item, appeared in the Chicago Tribune as 'MYSTERIOUS TRIPLE MURDER' and in the Savannah Morning News under 'FOULLY MURDERED. A Gang of Desperadoes Kill a Family in Texas.'

Through late April and early May, weeklies in Wisconsin, Minnesota, New Jersey and Ohio cut the story to one or two sentences in crime digests, beside executions, lynchings and other killings. Repeated retelling changed the details: the young man appeared as Lease, Case, Lense and Lees, and the place as Frio, Trio and 'Littleton, Frio'. The papers called it 'the horrible act' and a 'Cold-Blooded Slaughter', but none offered an explanation.

The earliest Texas report placed the house 'on the Frio', while the St. Louis special and several digests named a town of 'Trio', probably a misprint, and one put it at 'Littleton, Frio'. The young man was named 'Case' in the Dallas Herald, 'Lense' in the Chicago Tribune and 'Lease' in most other versions.

reader.title: McLauren family killings, Edwards County, Texas
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: Reports describe an unexplained killing of a household by a band of about fifteen armed men, with no accusation, no stated race of victims or attackers and no stated motive (A1, A2, A5).

Three people were killed by a band of about fifteen men acting without any authority (A1, A3), but every report says no cause or motive was known (A2, A5), so nothing shows the killers acted under a pretext of justice, race or tradition.

All versions go back to one Uvalde report brought in by neighbors before particulars arrived (A1, A3); the wire and digest versions repeat its wording, and no independent local confirmation appears (A2, A12).

accounts.label: St. Louis special

framing.detail: Headlines called it 'CONCERTED MURDER', 'FOULLY MURDERED' and the work of 'A Gang of Desperadoes', and the text 'the horrible act'.
Northern and western papers ran the St. Louis special or the Express item in crime digests, often one sentence long, under headings like 'Tragical' and 'South'.

conflicts.note: The earliest, Texas-printed version (A1) says 'on the Frio'; 'Trio' is probably a transmission or typesetting variant.
Most versions print Lease; the spellings likely reflect telegraph and OCR errors.
